title: Negative edge correlation for forests and connected subgraphs: exhaustive checks, forests to 10 vertices and connected subgraphs to 9
statement: For every simple graph on at most 9 vertices (connected, for the connected-subgraph model) -- and, for the forest model alone, on at most 10 vertices -- and every pair of distinct edges e, f, the Rayleigh difference of the forest generating polynomial and of the connected-spanning-subgraph generating polynomial (with all edge weights equal to lambda) has only nonnegative coefficients in lambda; it is identically 0 when e and f lie in different blocks and positive at lambda = 1 when they lie in the same block. Hence the uniform forest and the uniform connected spanning subgraph, and their lambda-weighted versions for every lambda > 0, are edge-negatively correlated on all graphs with at most 9 vertices (forests: at most 10 vertices) (the pairwise-correlation part of Kahn's conjecture and Grimmett-Winkler Conjecture 1.1, which asks for negative association; their question (1.6) for all lambda). The same holds on all multigraphs of multiplicity <= 3 over 2-connected 6-vertex graphs and of multiplicity <= 2 over 2-connected 7-vertex graphs (every pair of edge copies, checked once per pair of edge classes by symmetry). Proved (written argument): for every matroid and distinct elements e, f, the independence-polynomial Rayleigh difference is N lambda^c + O(lambda^{c+1}), where c is the least size of a circuit containing e and f and N the number of such circuits (identically 0 if none); for graphs, P_Z = N lambda^{L-2} + O(lambda^{L-1}) with L the shortest cycle length through e and f, so the weighted forest measure is strictly negatively correlated at all sufficiently small lambda for edges in a common block. Dually (bond matroid), the connected-subgraph Rayleigh polynomial has top term N* lambda^{2m - c* - 2}, with c* the least size of a bond containing e and f and N* the number of such bonds, so that measure is strictly negatively correlated for all sufficiently large lambda.
resolves: nothing; extends the exhaustive evidence for the forest conjecture from Grimmett-Winkler's range (<= 8 vertices, or 9 vertices with <= 18 edges) to all graphs with <= 10 vertices and to all lambda > 0, and gives the first exhaustive evidence we found for the connected-subgraph conjecture (<= 9 vertices)
verified: check_forest_nc.py: the contraction + subset-recursion polynomials equal direct enumeration on all edge pairs of 2-connected graphs on <= 5 vertices and on random multigraphs; block factorisation; the shipped list of 538 2-connected graphs on 3..7 vertices has the OEIS A002218 counts and is pairwise non-isomorphic (n <= 6 checked by brute force); both conjectures coefficientwise on all graphs with <= 6 vertices; the recorded C run summaries are consistent (pure Python).
fnc.c / cnc.c over geng -C (nauty 2.8.8): 1, 3, 10, 56, 468, 7123, 194066 graphs on 3..9 vertices, 35,208,345 edge pairs per model, zero violations (evidence/forest_nc_runs.json).

fnc4.c over geng -Cq 10 r/500 (nauty 2.8.8), forests only: all 9,743,542 2-connected 10-vertex graphs (OEIS A002218) and all 2,570,347,998 pairs of distinct edges, zero violations (no negative coefficient, no P(1) <= 0, no P negative anywhere on (0, infinity)); 500 residue classes, 13 of them empty; min normalised margin 2.202e-07 at ICQrThiHw e=0-3 f=1-4. About 8 CPU-hours. fnc4.c is validated against the reference fnc.c by validate_fnc4.sh: identical per-pair output on all 2-connected graphs with 4..8 vertices (3/10/56/468/7123 graphs, 32/241/2497/34762/827929 output lines). The graph total is reconfirmed by geng alone and the pair total by an independent pass summing m(m-1)/2 over the same enumeration (evidence/raw/n10_crosschecks.txt).

fnc.c / cnc.c in multigraph mode over multig: 1,450,016 multigraphs (n = 6, multiplicity <= 3; 100,776,619 edge-class pairs, i.e. 381,037,850 edge-copy pairs) and 2,016,427 multigraphs (n = 7, multiplicity <= 2; 213,200,562 edge-class pairs, 461,730,002 edge-copy pairs), zero violations.
brute_force_crosscheck.py / brute_force_multigraph.py: the C tools agree with subset enumeration on 4,208 simple-graph pairs (connected graphs, n <= 6) per model and on 88,990 multigraph pair checks.

argument section 4 + check_forest_nc.py SMALL_LAMBDA_LAW: the small-lambda law on all edge pairs of 2-connected graphs with <= 6 vertices and on random binary/ternary matroids; offline checks on all 37,531 pairs with <= 7 vertices (C output vs independent cycle enumeration) and 5,040 random-matroid pairs.

Independent review (fresh agent, own big-integer DP over an edge ordering without contraction, validated against subset enumeration): exact polynomial agreement with fnc/cnc on all 538 2-connected graphs with 3..7 vertices (37,531 pairs per model), 301 sampled 8-vertex and 103 sampled 9-vertex graphs (including K9), and sampled multigraph families; all evidence counts recomputed from geng. Its provenance remark led to rerunning the 9-vertex runs with the shipped sources (0.2.0).

Independent review of section 4 and Corollary 2 (fresh agent): proofs judged sound; own code tested the full multivariate statement on 8,898 element pairs of random vector matroids over GF(2), GF(3), GF(5) (with loops and parallels), 7,308 multigraph pairs and 42 uniform matroids, and Corollary 2 on 25,486 pairs of random connected multigraphs with bonds found directly; 0 failures. Its minor fixes (converse direction, non-cancellation, citation of the component fact, loops) are applied in 0.2.1.

na_scan.py + check_forest_nc.py NA_SMALL: negative association beyond pairs at lambda = 1, in exact integer arithmetic, on all 2-connected graphs with 4..6 vertices for every pair of nontrivial up-sets on disjoint edge sets of sizes (3,3) and (4,2) (318,120,000 up-set pairs per model), no positive covariance for forests or connected subgraphs; positive control detects association.

check_forest_nc.py RAW_PROVENANCE: every count in evidence/forest_nc_runs.json is re-derived from the raw run outputs shipped in evidence/raw/ and must match exactly; perturbing one recorded total by 1 makes both RAW_PROVENANCE and EVIDENCE_SUMMARY fail.
unresolved: connected spanning subgraphs on 10 vertices (not run: cnc.c has no analogue of the fnc4.c speed-up and is already about 2.5x slower than it on 8 vertices), and either model on 11 or more vertices
general real edge weights (Grimmett-Winkler (1.7)) and negative association beyond the small exact scan (n <= 6, event supports (3,3) and (4,2), lambda = 1)
nonclaims: no proof is claimed; this dossier is evidence only

coefficientwise nonnegativity in lambda is checked, which is stronger than the conjectures require; nothing is claimed about graphs with more than 10 vertices, nor about the connected-subgraph model on more than 9
not a novelty determination: arXiv:2610.00549 reports unspecified exact coefficientwise computations that may overlap
the small-lambda law is likely known to specialists; it is recorded with proof, not as a novelty claim, and it says nothing about lambda = 1
smallest_decisive_test: A graph and two edges with P_X(1) < 0 (a counterexample), or a negative coefficient (which would still leave the conjecture open at that graph unless P_X takes a negative value on (0, infinity)).
